html:
Ibadan was a Yoruba city-state in what is now south-western Nigeria, founded around 1829 as a war camp and by the 1850s the strongest military power in Yorubaland. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900. Today it is one of Africa's largest cities.

It grew out of the wars that followed the fall of the old Oyo empire. Soldiers and refugees gathered on its hills, and the city was ruled not by a sacred king but by its war chiefs. Around 1840 Ibadan stopped the southward advance of the Sokoto Caliphate from Ilorin at the battle of Osogbo.

Ibadan then built an empire over other Yoruba towns, which in 1877 rose against it in the long Kiriji war. The British of Lagos helped broker peace, and in 1893 Ibadan signed a treaty accepting British protection.
